clue.text: Describing dialogue, excluding relations?

definitions.meaning: Plato wrote his philosophy as dialogues, and those works carry his name as an adjective
a friendship with no sexual relations is called by this name

explanation.surface: A grammarian asks what word fits a conversation that leaves out family members.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Relations' looks like relatives; it means sexual relations.
explanation.definitionFit: The adjective names both the dialogues of the Greek philosopher Plato and love that stays non-sexual.

clue.text: 'Last word in service' written about copper showing keenness

indicators.note: one word written around another encloses it

parts.note: a prayer in a church service ends with amen
Cu is the chemical symbol for copper

explanation.surface: A church sign about a copper roof shows enthusiasm for the closing prayer.
explanation.definitionFit: Acumen is sharpness of mind, a synonym for keenness of judgement.

clue.text: Shocking line I had, ringing you at last, right?

indicators.note: the outer letters encircle the others as a ring does

parts.note: I'd is the contraction of I had

indicators.note: at last picks the final letter of the word you

explanation.surface: A caller asks whether a startling remark they made when phoning was correct.
explanation.walkthrough: L and ID enclose UR, the last letter of 'you' plus R for 'right'.
explanation.definitionFit: Lurid means sensational or shocking, as in lurid headlines.

clue.text: What St. George needs if dragon's rampaging?

indicators.note: a rampaging beast throws things into disorder, so these letters are scrambled

explanation.surface: Facing a raging dragon, the patron saint of England would need to keep calm.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dragon's' is read as 'dragons', so IF DRAGONS is the fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: Coolness under danger is exactly what a dragon-slaying knight requires.

clue.text: Camping hotshots maybe securing first of lines which reach a long way?

parts.note: camping is done in a tent

indicators.note: to secure is to hold fast, so one piece encloses another

parts.note: aces are top performers or hotshots

indicators.note: first of picks the opening letter of lines

explanation.surface: Star campers grab long ropes that stretch far.
explanation.walkthrough: 'maybe' flags that camping hotshots is only loosely tent aces.
explanation.definitionFit: An octopus's long limbs extend far from its body to grasp things.

clue.text: Stops after cutting 100 inches?

indicators.note: the word for stops, once something is cut from it, loses letters

parts.note: ceases means stops
C is the Roman numeral for 100

explanation.surface: A tailor halts after trimming a hundred inches off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'inches' looks like a measurement noun; it is a verb meaning moves slowly.
explanation.definitionFit: To inch along is to move gradually, a synonym of eases forward.

clue.text: Hide article tragic hero wants to hold

indicators.note: one word holding another contains it

parts.note: King Lear is the tragic hero of Shakespeare's play
the is the definite article

explanation.surface: A tragic hero longs to clutch some concealed item.
explanation.definitionFit: A hide is an animal skin, which when tanned becomes this material.

clue.text: Unacceptable to have one blocking opinion

indicators.note: one piece blocking another sits in its middle

parts.note: not on is a British idiom for unacceptable
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: It is not right for someone to obstruct a view held by others.
explanation.definitionFit: A notion is an idea or belief, a synonym of opinion.

clue.text: Superfluous to seize spades, having little vegetation?

indicators.note: seizing something means holding it inside

parts.note: spare means extra or superfluous
S is the card-suit abbreviation for spades

explanation.surface: A gardener with extra tools grabs spades for thin land.
explanation.definitionFit: Sparse vegetation is thinly scattered, so the land has few plants.

clue.text: Inferior marine vehicle caught in water flow

parts.note: a sub is a submarine

indicators.note: the letter for caught goes inside the word for water flow

parts.note: a jet is a stream of water
C is the cricket abbreviation for caught

explanation.surface: A lesser submarine gets trapped in a powerful current.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone subject to another is subordinate or lower in rank.

clue.text: Some of the art here reveals connection with the ground?

indicators.note: Some of says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A gallery visitor finds part of the exhibition shows a link to the soil.
explanation.definitionFit: An electrical earth is the wire connecting a circuit to the ground.

clue.text: Chinaware represented Alice in blue material

indicators.note: one piece sits inside the other

parts.note: blue means smutty, so blue material is porn

indicators.note: represented means presented again in a new form, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Alice appears depicted on blue fabric.
explanation.walkthrough: 'blue' here means smutty, not the colour; 'represented' signals that Alice's letters are rearranged before going inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Fine china is another name for this translucent ceramic ware.

clue.text: Guy and a second guy capturing Arab boat

parts.note: cat is slang for a guy or fellow

indicators.note: capturing means holding inside

parts.note: man is another word for a guy
Ar is an abbreviation for Arab or Arabic

explanation.surface: Two men seize an Arab on a boat.
explanation.definitionFit: A catamaran is a twin-hulled sailing vessel.

clue.text: Suggest strongbox should not be opened

indicators.note: a word not opened has lost its first letter

parts.note: a coffer is a strongbox

explanation.surface: Advice that a safe must stay locked.
explanation.definitionFit: To offer an idea is to put it forward, or suggest it.

clue.text: Think about island waste?

indicators.note: about means around, so one piece goes round the other

parts.note: to muse is to think

explanation.surface: Reflect on the barren isle.
explanation.definitionFit: To misuse resources is to waste them.

clue.text: American educational centre? Fool ending in college in English city

parts.note: berk is British slang for a fool

indicators.note: the letter goes inside the city

parts.note: Ely is a cathedral city in Cambridgeshire

indicators.note: ending in picks the last letter of college

explanation.surface: A clue asks about a US university, then mocks a foolish student in an English town.
explanation.definitionFit: The University of California campus at Berkeley is a famous seat of learning.

clue.text: Object mostly accepted by parrot with good grace

indicators.note: something accepted by another is taken inside it

parts.note: Polly is a traditional name for a pet parrot

indicators.note: mostly means losing the final letter

parts.note: an item is an object

explanation.surface: A parrot graciously takes most of a thing it is offered.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing something politely is doing it courteously, with good grace.

clue.text: Article encapsulating specialist chef's gear?

indicators.note: encapsulating means enclosing

parts.note: an is the indefinite article
a pro is a professional or specialist

explanation.surface: An item describes a specialist cook's equipment.
explanation.definitionFit: A cook wears this garment to protect clothes in the kitchen.

clue.text: River, most half-hearted, slopping around

indicators.note: liquid slopping around is jumbled about, so the letters are scrambled

explanation.surface: A river described as listless as it washes about.
explanation.definitionFit: The personification of London's River Thames, a traditional nickname for it.

clue.text: Slight cut clipped craft as island arrived at

indicators.note: cut means trimmed of its last letter

parts.note: an insult is a slight

indicators.note: clipped means shortened at the end

parts.note: an ark is a boat or craft

explanation.surface: A trimmed boat lands at an island.
explanation.definitionFit: Insular comes from the Latin for island and means of or like one.

clue.text: Board having reserve after company beginning to face cost in large volume

indicators.note: after puts the board and reserve pieces later in the answer
beginning to picks the first letter of face

parts.note: a fee is a cost
a table is a board
to book is to reserve

explanation.surface: A board with funds held back faces costs in a big ledger.
explanation.definitionFit: A coffee table book is a large illustrated volume meant for display.

clue.text: Majority will keep working when given one gem

indicators.note: keeping something means holding it inside

parts.note: most means the majority
on means working or operating

explanation.surface: Most will stay employed when each receives a jewel.
explanation.definitionFit: Moonstone is a pearly feldspar used as a gemstone.

clue.text: What's not being covered as a leisure pursuit?

definitions.text: What's not being covered as a leisure pursuit?

parts.words: What's not being covered as a leisure pursuit
parts.note: an uncovered recreation: going without clothes as a pastime, not leaving an unreported hobby

explanation.definitionFit: The practice of going unclothed for leisure is the naturist lifestyle.

clue.text: United wrong to pick up on identity of pitch

indicators.note: in a down clue picking up lifts the word so it reads upwards

parts.note: a sin is a wrong

explanation.surface: A football club, wronged, gets a ruling about its pitch.
explanation.definitionFit: Notes sung in unison share exactly the same pitch.

clue.text: Soldier clad in appropriate American gear

indicators.note: clad in means wrapped inside

parts.note: apt means appropriate
a para is a paratrooper

explanation.surface: A soldier dressed in suitable US kit.
explanation.definitionFit: Apparatus is equipment, a synonym of gear.

clue.text: Dangerous fish near, circling river area

indicators.note: circling means surrounding

parts.note: near is old slang for mean or stingy

explanation.surface: A deadly fish lurks nearby, swimming round a river.
explanation.walkthrough: 'near' looks like close by; it means tight-fisted.
explanation.definitionFit: The stingray has a venomous barbed tail.

clue.text: No longer saucy in the buff?

parts.note: ex means former, no longer
pert means cheeky or saucy

explanation.surface: Someone once cheeky now stands naked.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in the buff' looks like naked; a buff is an enthusiast, hence skilled.
explanation.definitionFit: A buff is a knowledgeable enthusiast, so being one makes you skilled.

clue.text: One puts in excited "Yes" receiving item from fiancé

indicators.note: receiving means taking inside
excited means stirred up, so the letters are mixed

parts.note: an engagement ring is given by a fiancé

explanation.surface: An excited yes greets the gift of a ring.
explanation.walkthrough: 'excited' turns YES into SYE, which receives RING.
explanation.definitionFit: A syringe injects fluid, so it puts things into the body.

clue.text: Cry going up about wrecked cab? One supplies images for site

indicators.note: about here means positioned around, so the reversed cry wraps round the wrecked cab
in a down clue going up reads the word upwards

parts.note: a mew is a cry, as of a gull or cat

indicators.note: wrecked means smashed up, so the letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: A shout goes up around a crashed taxi.
explanation.walkthrough: 'going up' reverses the cry, since down clues read upwards; 'wrecked' scrambles cab, and that scramble sits within the reversal.
explanation.definitionFit: A webcam is a camera feeding pictures to a website.

clue.text: Allowed to go topless, with dreadful consequences

indicators.note: going topless means losing the first letter

parts.note: lawful means allowed

explanation.surface: Topless sunbathing was permitted, with terrible results.
explanation.definitionFit: Awful describes something terrible in effect.
